collection.description: Should a villager grab it, or step carefully around it?

ask.text:
On moonless nights, the beach comes alive with ghost crabs: pale, see-through things that scuttle sideways and vanish down holes in the sand. The elders say each one carries something someone lost, a word, a memory, a name, and that whoever catches one gets back what it carries, or loses something new to it.
(Name) is walking home along the beach in the dark, and the sand around (his/her) feet is crawling with them. One stops right in front of (him/her) and raises its claws. Should (name) grab it, or step carefully around it?

text_only.reason: the word in the owner's story; what changes in the game is the ending's own EFFECT line (the ledger), so this word alone changes nothing

c1o1.text: The nip goes cold all the way up (his/her) arm and into (his/her) head, and (name) drops the crab, which scuttles off into its hole. On the walk home, (name) realises (he/she) can't remember what (he/she) is called. The crab has taken it, down into the sand. The village calls (him/her) "?" and some of the children go out with buckets every moonless night after that, trying to catch it back.

c1o2.text: The crab goes still in (name)'s hands, and then crumbles into pale sand that blows up into (his/her) face. (Name) sneezes three times. In the morning, (his/her) face is different: not younger, not older, just someone else's, a face someone on this island lost long ago. The elders look at (him/her) for a long time and one of them starts to cry, and won't say why.

c1.text: (Name) lunges and catches the crab in both hands. It's cold, colder than the night, and it nips (his/her) thumb hard...

c2o1.text: (Name) picks (his/her) way all along the beach without touching a single crab, and gets home with every word, memory and name (he/she) left with. (He/She) lies awake for a while, wondering what the crab would have given back. In the morning, there is a small pale shell on (his/her) doorstep, and nothing inside it.

c2o2.text: One crab follows (name) all the way home, clicking. It sits outside the door all night. In the morning it's gone, and so is (name)'s old name. A new one has been left in its place, as if the crab had been carrying it for someone, and decided (name) would do. Everyone calls (him/her) (made1), and nobody remembers ever calling (him/her) anything else.

c2.text: (Name) steps carefully around the crab, and another, and another. The whole beach seems to shift around (him/her), clicking softly...
